text:
Marta V: Heads-up — noticed a weird interaction between the 'anchor_version' field and automatic rollback. A canary hit errors and the system rolled back to an older pinned model instead of the last healthy one.
Alex C: oof. do you have the rollout metadata?
Marta V: pasted below from logs:
```json
{"model":"text-redwood-3b","rollout":{"strategy":"anchored","anchor_version":"v2.9.0","soft_ttl":86400,"rollback_policy":"auto","last_healthy":"v2.8.7"}}
```
Marta V: When the canary failed, the control loop picked anchor_version (v2.9.0) as the fallback target. That was unexpected — we thought anchor should be a hint, not a strict fallback.
Jay P: Hmm, that suggests we conflated "anchor" with "preferred stable". We intended anchor to be the pinned version for route affinity, not the canonical rollback target.
Sara L: Agree. In the current metadata surface we have no explicit "rollback_target" or priority list, so the controller picks the first matching pinned version.
Alex C: What are tradeoffs if we add rollback_target vs preserving current semantics?
Jay P: If we add explicit rollback_target, ops can declare exactly where to go on failure, which is safest for critical tenants. Downsides: more fields to maintain and more UI/UX surface in Console. Also migration complexity for older routes.
Marta V: Another option: define rollback precedence order array: ["last_healthy","rollback_target","anchor_version","global_default"]. That keeps anchor as lower priority.
Sara L: I like precedence arrays; it's explicit and extendable. We should also expose TTL semantics: soft_ttl vs hard_ttl. Right now soft_ttl only affects traffic shifting, not rollback eligibility.
Alex C: Could we do a minimal compatibility change: treat anchor as low-priority fallback and introduce a new optional field "fallback_priority": ["last_healthy","anchor_version"] for customers who care? That keeps default safe.
Jay P: Minimal changes are attractive. But we should also add a controller invariant: never rollback to a version older than last_healthy unless explicit override is set. That prevents regressions.
Sara L: Implementation note: controller currently computes candidate set by matching pinned models across namespaces, then sorts by timestamp. We'll need to extend comparator to consult precedence list.
Marta V: UX: Console should show effective fallback order and allow per-rollout override. If not set, show inferred order and a warning if anchor is older than last_healthy.
Alex C: For storage/schema: keep rollout metadata as top-level map; add optional array field "fallback_order" and optional bool "allow_anchor_as_fallback". Keep defaults to preserve behavior for existing routes.
Marta V: Sample suggested schema snippet:```yaml
rollout:
  strategy: anchored
  anchor_version: v2.9.0
  last_healthy: v2.8.7
  fallback_order: [last_healthy, rollback_target, anchor_version, global_default]
  allow_anchor_as_fallback: false
  soft_ttl: 86400
  hard_ttl: 2592000
```
Jay P: We should also version the rollout schema (e.g., rollout.schema_version = "2026-03-1") and allow the controller to run migration logic. That avoids surprise behavior during rollout of this change.
Sara L: +1 to schema_version. For migration path: if schema_version missing, treat as legacy and apply safe defaults (fallback_order = [last_healthy, global_default], allow_anchor_as_fallback=false).
Alex C: Operational concern: what about cross-region failovers where anchor_version isn't available in target region? The fallback system must include compatibility semantics (model variant mapping). Maybe fallback candidates should be model fingerprint pairs, not just version strings.
Marta V: Good call. We already have variant mapping for quantized builds; reuse that: candidate = {model_id, variant_id, region_constraints}. But that's an internal representation — keep rollout metadata simple while controller expands candidates.
Jay P: Action items: 1) spec PR for rollout metadata changes (schema_version, fallback_order, allow_anchor_as_fallback, optional rollback_target). 2) Controller change: enforce never-fallback-to-older-than-last_healthy unless explicit override, consult fallback_order. 3) Console: show effective fallback chain and migration warnings. 4) Add unit+integration tests for cross-region/variant cases.
Sara L: I'll own the spec PR. Will include examples and migration notes.
Marta V: I'll add controller test cases and a small RFC blurb for oncall.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-controller v1.42 -> staging (hash: d4f9a2). :rocket:
Alex C: Thanks all. Let's try to avoid adding a new field for every edgecase; prefer an explicit precedence array and a schema_version. That keeps future changes manageable.
Jay P: One more thought — add an audit marker when controller chooses a fallback that is not the most recent stable: that helps postmortems.
Marta V: Yes, audit + event: "fallback_selected" with candidate list and reasons.
Sara L: added to TODOs in the PR.
Alex C: Great. No blocker for the canary rollback today then?
Marta V: Canary reverted and redeployed to v2.8.9 manually. Opening PR now.
Jay P: Thanks — lean and safe approach. :thumbsup:
